name: Bromsgrove town loop
blurb: An easy spin round the town: the High Street, Sidemoor, Charford and Aston Fields.

name: Stoke Pound and the Queen's Head
blurb: Down to the canal at Stoke Pound for the Queen's Head, back by Tardebigge's famous locks.

name: Upton Warren flats
blurb: The flattest ride here: out past Stoke Heath to Upton Warren and back by Stoke Prior.

name: Tardebigge church climb
blurb: Up to Tardebigge's hilltop church above the lock flight, and down through Burcot.

name: The Lickey Hills
blurb: Woods and steep lanes: Blackwell, Barnt Green, Cofton Hackett, Rednal and over the Lickeys.

name: Clent Hills
blurb: The big one: Fairfield and Belbroughton, up to Clent and the Nimmings, back over Romsley.

name: Dodford lanes
blurb: Quiet lanes west of town: Timberhonger, Dodford, Bournheath and back through Sidemoor.

name: Romsley and Frankley
blurb: Rolling country on the edge of Birmingham: Rubery, Frankley, Romsley and Hunnington.

name: Grand tour
blurb: The whole map in one: the canal at Stoke Pound, Tardebigge, the Lickeys, the Clent Hills and home.

name: Clent KOM repeats
blurb: Three times up the Clent Hills: St Kenelm's Pass from Clent village, then down Hagley Wood Lane and round again.

name: Winwood Heath wall
blurb: Romsley's monster, twice. A 3 km warm-up mostly downhill by Shut Mill Lane to the bottom, then up Winwood Heath Road, 1.1 km at 10%; round by Romsley and again.

name: Lickey Beacon climbs
blurb: The Lickeys' steepest: Rose Hill, Beacon Lane and Mearse Lane, with the woods all round.

name: The Worcestershire Epic
blurb: The big day out, every major climb: the canal at Stoke Pound, Tardebigge, Mearse Lane, Beacon Lane and Rose Hill on the Lickeys, Winwood Heath, St Kenelm's Pass and Hagley Wood Lane on the Clents, home by Belbroughton and Dodford.
